quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering an interstate. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and match the traffic already on the highway. Then merge smoothly when it is safe.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed limit in a school zone is:

options.text: 30 mph.
20 mph.
15 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a school zone is 15 mph. Drive carefully in school zones where children may be present.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for trains coming from either direction.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Watch for trains from both directions. Be aware of vehicles like school buses and hazardous material trucks that must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They create vibration and sound to alert inattentive drivers that their vehicle has left the travel lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They create vibration and sound to alert inattentive drivers that their vehicle has left the travel lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: When approaching a curve in the road, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down before and during a curve. You can speed up again after you pass the middle of the turn.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, you must securely attach a note with your name, phone number, and address to the damaged vehicle or property.

questions.question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and go carefully.
Wait for a green light before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for traffic from other directions, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When stopped at a red traffic light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane, even if other lights are red. First, yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop Sign Ahead.
Side Road.
Railroad Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming ahead.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your car and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Stay at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop very quickly. If you follow too closely, you could hit the rider if they fall. This is especially dangerous on wet or icy roads, gravel, or metal surfaces like bridges.

questions.question: You have a minor collision at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries or deaths, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians clearly, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A side road ahead.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a side road is coming up ahead.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
To give the truck driver room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give the truck driver room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Never pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull in front of large vehicles before passing.
Because following too closely will catch you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, van, and trailer drivers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Stay back so you can see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: At night, oncoming headlights are blinding you. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your car safe until you pass the oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: What is the amount of alcohol in the blood called?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC number means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces all the abilities you need to drive safely. Alcohol travels from your stomach to your blood, then to other parts of your body. It affects the brain areas that control judgment and skill.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
On a curve with no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see ahead. Always assume an oncoming vehicle is out of sight. Pass only where signs and road markings permit it, and only if you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
You must turn right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road splits ahead. You must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: A safe driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always look at what is actually happening at the intersection. Be ready to yield if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: Your following distance should be ____ for every 10 miles per hour of speed.

options.text: One-half car length
One car length
Three car lengths

questions.correctAnswerText: One car length
questions.explanation: Keep at least one car length of space in front of you for every 10 miles per hour you are driving. As you go faster, you need more distance to stop. This space helps you avoid crashes if something unexpected happens.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to move back to the right lane:

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before moving back. Always check your blind spots before returning to your lane.

questions.question: When you see a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, whether or not there is a stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you about school zones. When you see these signs, stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must give you the right-of-way.
You must give them the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give them the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield to these pedestrians.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming toward them from the opposite direction. This includes cars, bicycles, and motorcycles.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit for safety, but never faster. Slow down for curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop completely.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at ramps and be ready for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic flow.
